A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ETTIN study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across formatting changes, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training evaluations, encoder–decoder and cross-objective comparisons, and WinoGender analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds the MMLU CS and GSM8k comparison in Table 5.

M1.justification: Architectures, pretraining objectives, and cross-objective procedures remain unchanged. The explicit MNTP explanation in v2 Section 3.5 already appeared in v1 Section 3.6, footnote 8; correcting nearby MLM wording clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds MMLU CS and GSM8k evaluations for 1B models in Table 5, extending coverage to harder classification and reasoning benchmarks. Training corpora and all previously evaluated tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in all matched experiments. Table 5 evaluates existing decoder and decoder-from-encoder variants on new benchmarks. The more explicit references to LLM2Vec do not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The added Table 5 comparison uses a restricted design: only 1B decoder and decoder-from-encoder models, unlike the multi-size, four-variant comparison in Figure 1. Existing training budgets, evaluation settings, and fine-tuning sweeps are retained.

E4.justification: The cross-objective analyses, scaling comparisons, and WinoGender case study are retained without substantive changes. Table 5 adds benchmark coverage, rather than a separate ablation, sensitivity test, or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: WinoGender accuracy and standard-error reporting are unchanged between v1 Table 9 and v2 Table 10. No new seed information, repeated-run reporting, uncertainty estimates, or formal significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports Decoder versus Dec-From-Enc scores of 27.0 versus 37.0 on MMLU CS and 32.0 versus 18.9 on GSM8k. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 scores. All eleven original tables retain their contents.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal theoretical results or proofs. Existing mathematical specifications are unchanged; the new discussion of CLM data efficiency is an explanatory hypothesis, not a derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same claims about the paired open-data model suite, competitive performance, objective-dependent strengths, cross-objective adaptation gaps, and released artifacts.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds a hypothesis that CLM's data efficiency at smaller training budgets explains disagreement with Gisserot-Boukhlef et al. v2 also interprets the new MMLU/GSM8k contrast and states that smaller models provide insufficient signal on these harder tasks.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies zero-shot, closed-book evaluation. Appendix G discloses LLM coding assistance and human verification. Hardware, hyperparameters, harness commit, and resource-access information remain unchanged; compute details are merely relocated to Appendix E.

R1.justification: v2 adds Nielsen et al. (2024) and Marone et al. (2025, mmBERT). It also explicitly discusses disagreement with the already-cited Gisserot-Boukhlef et al. study, refining research positioning without changing the central contribution.

P1.justification: Limited copyediting and paragraph revisions accompany moving compute configuration to Appendix E, promoting the MNTP footnote into the main text, and adding an LLM-usage appendix. The overall narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5, shortens Figure 1's caption, and adopts ICLR title, heading, and running-header formatting with associated reflow. Existing appendix tables are renumbered and repositioned; their structures and the three figures remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: Table 5 modestly strengthens evidence about task-dependent performance on harder benchmarks. Clearer MNTP and evaluation descriptions and engagement with conflicting research improve clarity and context while preserving prior evidence. The gains are limited: the new comparison covers only two 1B variants without uncertainty estimates, and the proposed data-efficiency explanation is not directly tested.
